verdicts.reason: A keeps the image-left/text-right split and a strong headline, but the CTA is put above the headline at top right, so the reading order is broken. The 'Clinically tested' eyebrow is moved below the subcopy and enlarged. The legal text is microscopic and the logo is so big it competes with the headline. The jar is shrunk and pulled out of the leaf image. B crops the leaves into a thin strip and floats the CTA above it, cut off from the copy. The jar is shrunk to an unreadable thumbnail at bottom left and the logo is small, and both are scattered along the bottom row with tiny unreadable legal text. The eyebrow again sits under the subcopy, and the product and brand presence are lost far more than in A.
